summary: Iteration 3 — role gating on /api/chantiers (POST/PATCH = admin|commercial, DELETE = admin only), POST /api/auth/push-token (set + clear with null), best-effort Expo push on PATCH assigned_to, GET /api/stats/company (admin-only, company-isolated). 63/63 pytest tests pass: 20 new iter3 tests + 43 regression tests from iter1 & iter2 (after a 2-line adjustment to test_multitenant.py to align with the new role rules).

minor.issue: Carry-over from iter2: still does NOT filter by company_id (server.py L571-573 only matches by id), while export.json correctly does (L644). Cross-tenant PDF download possible by UUID guess.
Carry-over: returns 200 {'ok': true} even when mesure does not exist (no 404).
Carry-over: silent 200 no-op when id is unknown or belongs to another company.

Always returns 200 even with empty body (push_token defaults to None due to Optional). This effectively means an empty POST clears the token — usable but a bit surprising; consider requiring the field explicitly.
Carry-over: 'module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' on startup. Functional but noisy.
Carry-over: returns 200 OK on creation; REST convention is 201.

action_items: Optional: add company_id filter to GET /api/chantiers/{id}/export.pdf to match export.json (iter2 residual gap, still present in iter3).
Optional: return 404 on DELETE /api/feedbacks/{id} and DELETE /api/mesures/{id} when nothing was deleted.
Optional carry-over: pin bcrypt<4 / upgrade passlib, return 201 on creation endpoints.
Consider requiring an explicit push_token field on POST /api/auth/push-token (currently an empty body silently clears the token).
critical_code_review_comments: require_roles(['admin','commercial']) correctly gates POST and PATCH /api/chantiers — technician returns 403 with FR message.
require_roles(['admin']) correctly gates DELETE /api/chantiers — commercial AND technician return 403.
POST /api/mesures remains gated only by auth_user (no role check) — all three demo roles can create mesures.
send_push_to_user is properly best-effort: short-circuits when user has no push_token, and the outer try/except in httpx call swallows every exception. Logs warnings only.
PATCH /api/chantiers correctly triggers push only when new assigned_to differs from existing.get('assigned_to') — no spurious notifications on unrelated edits.

GET /api/stats/company correctly: (1) admin-only via require_admin, (2) filtered by company_id on chantiers, mesures (via $in chantier ids of the company), and users. Verified zero-state for a fresh company and aggregation after one chantier + one alerted mesure (closure_rate=100.0, by_technician populated).
by_status is initialized to {devis_a_faire:0, technique_a_valider:0, cloture:0} so all 3 keys are always present.
by_technician sorts by mesures desc and names 'Non affecté' for unassigned — clean.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_multitenant.py (2-line fix: test_acme_chantier_invisible_to_default_admin now creates via acme_admin and cleans via acme_admin, since iter3 forbids technicians from creating/deleting chantiers)
seed_data_creation: Each test class uses its own ephemeral users (TEST_acme_*, TEST_acme_admin_*) and chantiers (TEST_*) created via fixtures, with teardown that DELETEs created chantiers as admin. Demo users and 5 seeded default-company chantiers were left intact. Tech user's push_token is set/cleared during tests but always reset to null at the end of TestPatchAssignmentPushBestEffort.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green (63/63). Iter3 endpoints validated: role gating on /api/chantiers, /api/auth/push-token, /api/stats/company (shape + admin-only + company isolation). Push best-effort verified by patching assigned_to to a user with no token (no error). Test fixture for acme_user is still a technician — when adding tests that need acme to CREATE/DELETE chantiers, use acme_admin instead. Next iteration should focus on frontend wiring of the stats screen and push registration flow.
rca_of_issue: Single regression observed and fixed in-test: TestChantierIsolation.test_acme_chantier_invisible_to_default_admin used acme_user (technician) to POST a chantier; iter3 added require_roles(['admin','commercial']) on that route, so the call now returns 403. Adjusted the test to use acme_admin for both POST and the cleanup DELETE. No production code changed.
